title: Failure Cascade
body:
Machines depend on each other. A dependency A B T means machine A depends on machine B: T seconds after B fails, A fails too (unless it has already failed).

Machine X fails at time 0. Find how many machines fail in total (count X itself) and the time at which the last one fails.

Function to complete

Complete failureCascade(start, machine, dependsOn, time). It returns two numbers: how many machines fail and the time of the last failure.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: The first line contains M (the number of dependencies) and the name X. Each of the next M lines contains A B T.
out: Two integers: the number of failed machines and the time of the last failure.
cons: Machine names are strings without spaces; a pair may appear more than once

samples.in:
3 X
A X 2
B A 3
C X 10
samples.ex: A fails at 2, B at 5, C at 10. Four machines fail, the last at time 10.
Q fails at 4. R does not depend on anything that failed, so it keeps running.

hidden.in:
4 X
A X 5
A X 2
B A 1
B X 10

if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    _m = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    start = _t[_p]; _p += 1
    machine = []; dependsOn = []; time = []
    for _ in range((_m)):
        machine.append(_t[_p + 0])
        dependsOn.append(_t[_p + 1])
        time.append(int(_t[_p + 2]))
        _p += 3
    _r = Solution().failureCascade(start, machine, dependsOn, time)
    print(" ".join(map(str, _r)))
